claim: Mao et al. set the amount of synthetic class-label noise and box noise with two separate parameters.
gold_sentence: We use two parameters, NLabel and NBBox, to control the level of symmetric class label noise and uniform bounding box localization noise, respectively.

claim: Li et al.'s noise-resistant training only helps when the labels are noisy; on clean annotations it gives no gain.
gold_sentence: On clean training data with 0% annotation noise, our method can still improve upon vanilla training by +1.9% in mAP.
notes: sentence: +1.9% mAP even on clean data

claim: Simply mixing pseudo labels with the ground truth does not let a standard Faster R-CNN make good use of them.
gold_sentence: The combination of ground truth and pseudo labels gives more information to train the object detector, but a regular FasterRCNN could not learn from these priors appropriately.

claim: Objects left unlabelled give the network a wrong training signal that can badly hurt its accuracy.
gold_sentence: This would provide an incorrect training signal to the neural network which could deteriorate its performance by a large margin.

claim: Adding box-level labels to classification data is a practical way to improve large-scale detection.
gold_sentence: With boundingbox supervision, R-FCN-3000 was able to obtain 18% better performance, suggesting that obtaining box-level supervision on classification data is a practical way of improving large scale object detection.

claim: Fully supervised detectors keep almost the same accuracy however many instance labels are missing.
gold_sentence: The performance of all FSOD methods drops significantly as the missing rate increases, which demonstrates that the performance of FSOD techniques is considerably affected by the quality of the training set.
notes: sentence: all FSOD methods drop significantly

claim: Dealing with annotation noise matters for developing robust detection algorithms.
gold_sentence: Our findings highlight the importance of addressing annotation noise and its impact on the development of robust detection algorithms.

claim: One existing method reduces box localization noise by refining the annotations in alternating steps.
gold_sentence: Mao et al. [27] proposed a framework that mitigates localization noise by alternating refinement.

claim: Mao et al.'s refinement framework only helps with box localization noise, not with class label noise.
gold_sentence: The experimental results confirm that our proposal can significantly alleviate the negative impact caused by noisy annotations, despite the type of noise.
notes: sentence: works despite the type of noise

claim: Learning detectors from incompletely annotated images is an emerging and difficult research problem.
gold_sentence: Training object detectors with incompleteness of annotations is a new rising and challenging vision problem that aims to learn a robust detector by recalibrating the incorrect training signal with partial annotations.

claim: Mao et al. identify wrong training labels by judging noise across training iterations.
gold_sentence: On the basis of this finding, we proposed a noise-judging method, called cross-iteration noise judgment, to identify incorrect training labels.

claim: Noisy annotations make a detector more likely to confuse objects with the background.
gold_sentence: This degradation is particularly evident in high value of Bkg and Miss on TIDE measure, which indicate an increased tendency of the model to confuse between background and foreground classes.

claim: Changing how anchors are assigned to labels removes most of the accuracy loss caused by missing annotations.
gold_sentence: We train a Faster-RCNN with this label assignment scheme and evaluate its performance when it is trained with and without missing labels.
notes: sentence only says they evaluate it

claim: Training object detectors on noisy annotations has been studied as thoroughly as noisy labels in image classification.
gold_sentence: Unlike with the noisy label-supervised image classification, which has achieved many results [7, 10, 17, 20, 22, 27, 28], only a few studies have focused on the noisy annotationsupervised object detection.

claim: A simple way to find unlabelled objects is to run a detector trained on a fully annotated dataset such as COCO.
gold_sentence: To further take the incompleteness of annotations into account, one straight-forward way is to use other trained detector from well-annotated dataset (such as COCO [4]) to detect the presence of the amphibolous objects.

claim: Training detectors on imprecise boxes is still hard because the noise weakens the supervision signal.
gold_sentence: Due to the degenerated supervision introduced by noisy annotations, object detection with noisy bounding boxes remains a challenging problem.

claim: DISCO corrects the training signal by modelling how proposals are distributed in space.
gold_sentence: Our main contributions are listed as follows: (1) Motivated by the observation about proposal aggregation, we propose DISCO to calibrate supervision signals with spatial distribution modeling.

claim: Missing annotations mainly lower a detector's confidence scores, while its box placement stays fairly accurate.
gold_sentence: Notice how scores drop when the detector is trained with missing annotations, however, localization is still pretty good, even for the baseline detector!

claim: A detector trained on one dataset can usually be applied directly to a different dataset.
gold_sentence: It’s hard or even unpractical to directly transfer detectors from one dataset to another.

claim: A quick fix for missing labels is to only use anchors that overlap well with the existing ground-truth boxes.
gold_sentence: One quick solution is to perform IoU threshold by taking into account only the anchors with sufficient IoU values with the existing ground truth bounding boxes.

claim: Weighting gradients by overlap with the labelled boxes reduces the harm done by missing annotations.
gold_sentence: This gap can be further bridged with a simple overlap based gradient weighting function to reduce the ill effects of missing labels during training.

claim: Wrong class labels only affect classification and have no effect on how well a detector localises objects.
gold_sentence: Incorrect class tokens in object detection can lead to severe noise as it disrupts both the categorization and localization aspects.

claim: Li et al. correct noisy class labels using the model's own predictions.
gold_sentence: Inspired by the bootstrapping method [33], we use the classifiers’ predictions to update the noisy GT label.

claim: Even when a box label is noisy, the proposals matched to it tend to cluster around the object's true position.
gold_sentence: As shown in Figure 1(b), we observed that the real ground-truth is usually situated in the aggregation region of the proposals assigned to a noisy ground-truth, showing that the spatial distribution of proposals can act as a statistical prior for the potential locations of objects.

claim: All parts of Mao et al.'s method contribute to reducing the effect of wrong annotations.
gold_sentence: Each proposed step is experimentally shown to be effective in alleviating the negative impact caused by incorrect annotations.

claim: Class label noise and box noise can easily be corrected together in a single step.
gold_sentence: Due to the entanglement of an unknown mixture of label noise and bbox noise, it is diﬃcult to correct both types of annotation noise in a single step.
notes: sentence: difficult in a single step

claim: Xu et al.'s approach beats both fully and weakly supervised detectors across a range of missing-label rates.
gold_sentence: Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2007 and 2012 compared the improvement between fully and weakly supervised methods, and show that our method stands out among all of them at different levels of missing instance-level labels.

claim: Refining noisy boxes a second time gives tighter boxes than refining them only once.
gold_sentence: The first-time refined boxes can cover the objects more tightly than noisy ground-truths, and the second-time refinement can further contribute to more precise ones.

claim: Crowd-sourced or machine-made labels can contain wrong classes, badly placed boxes, missing boxes and spurious boxes.
gold_sentence: For example, Fig. 1 illustrates the four types of possible noise in crowd-sourcing or machine-generated labels; categorization noise (Fig. 1a), localization noise (Fig. 1b), missing annotation (Fig. 1c), and bogus bounding box noise (Fig. 1d).

claim: DISCO's advantage over other methods is largest when the box annotations are very noisy.
gold_sentence: Extensive experiments demonstrate that DISCO can achieve SOTA performance in this task, especially at high noise levels.

claim: Soft sampling raises detection scores over standard training when labels are missing, though some drop remains.
gold_sentence: Soft-sampling has significantly better detection scores compared to the baseline, although there is a noticable drop in scores here as well.

claim: Using pseudo labels when choosing negative proposals reduces the number of false background samples.
gold_sentence: A positive proposal as the regions which have a high IOU with any (ground truth or pseudo) instance label, while a negative proposal must has a small IOU with either instance labels.

claim: One earlier method handles noisy labels with meta-learning on a small set of clean examples.
gold_sentence: Xu et al. [43] proposed a meta-learning based approach that utilizes few clean samples.

claim: Different kinds of annotation noise start to amplify each other once noise levels are high.
gold_sentence: This suggests that at lower noise levels, the four noise types operate independently, while at higher noise levels, they start to overlap and exhibit synergistic effects.

claim: Soft labels make detectors more robust to missing annotations.
gold_sentence: We show that soft labels with well-adjusted temperature lead to better performance, even for a clean dataset with no annotation noise.
notes: sentence is about clean data, not missing labels

claim: Better label assignment alone, as in FreeAnchor, is not enough to cope with noisy boxes.
gold_sentence: Besides, even with better label assignment, FreeAnchor still underperforms in such a challenging task.

claim: Pixel-level segmentation masks take several times longer to annotate than bounding boxes.
Active learning can halve the number of images that need manual labelling for object detection.
Label noise harms instance segmentation models more than it harms object detectors.
Vision-language models such as CLIP can be used to automatically clean noisy detection labels.
Annotators are more likely to miss objects that are tiny or packed closely together.
gold_sentence: Missing annotation noise is easily generated when objects are small or crowded.
notes: was a none claim; the search found this sentence

claim: Asking several annotators per image and taking a majority vote reduces bounding box errors.
Synthetic images from game engines can replace manually annotated data for training detectors.
Label noise in 3D LiDAR object detection mostly comes from inaccurate box orientation.
Medical imaging datasets contain more annotation errors than natural image datasets.
Paying annotators more per image improves the accuracy of their bounding boxes.
Mosaic and mixup augmentation reduce the effect of label noise on YOLO detectors.
Video object detectors can use consistency across frames to correct noisy box labels.
Annotation tools that suggest boxes automatically speed up labelling without reducing box accuracy.
